name: The Great Eastern Home
description: The Great Eastern Home, rooted in 176 years of history since its establishment as The Great Eastern Mills in 1839, embodies a blend of heritage and artistry. Located in Byculla, Mumbai, it preserves its architectural charm, showcasing high ceilings, wooden beams, and exposed brick walls. The space displays a curated collection of fine furniture and collectibles, inspired by Baroque, Art Nouveau, Art Deco, and Colonial styles, emphasizing timeless elegance. The store celebrates craftsmanship and hybrid design influences, collaborating with renowned designers to balance classical aesthetics with contemporary trends. It also promotes art, offering a platform for artists and sculptors to exhibit their works.

featured_reviews.name: Sky & Patty Williamson
featured_reviews.review_text: I had the good fortune of finding Natesan’s beautiful collection a few years ago and was delighted to return on my recent visit to Mumbai in March 2026.  The showroom is two levels, a beautifully curated display of original antiquities for viewing on the first floor and an equally beautiful and intriguing display of finest quality reproductions and non antique vintage pieces available for purchase on the second floor.  The collection was quite diverse with brass and bronze hindu statues, wood carved pieces, and artwork - stunning.  A wide range of sizes and pricepoints are also available and at good value given the very high quality of the pieces.  I had a wonderful discussion of the various pieces with Pushpa who was very charming and extremely knowledgeable about the history and artistic styles.  This is a no pressure environment and i would have viewed the visit alone as a highpoint, though i was thrilled to take home a beautiful Kerala mural.  Pushpa was very helpful in talking through the transport options and it was a seamless and easy transaction.  Definitely make a visit to Natesan’s a priority on your next Mumbai visit.  Cheers! Patty

name: Mysore Creation
description:
Mysore Creation, founded in 1958 by Shri. A.R. Nikam, is a celebration of master craftsmanship in Indian Handicrafts. Being a craftsman himself, he aimed at promoting and uplifting under his able guidance artists from South India, thus giving raw talent a fulfilling direction.
Mysore Creation aims to represent the finesse and divine aspect of Indian Handicrafts.
Endless hours of designing and experimental use of raw materials resulted in a beautiful confluence of creativity to bring about the Grandeur of Indian Mythology.
While we strive to continue the legacy, we hope our journey attracts people who understand and appreciate the splendor of Indian Art.

featured_reviews.name: Nirupama Kadam
featured_reviews.review_text:
To me Mysore Creation is not just a store but an enriching experience each time I visit it.
A wide range of artifacts both period and contemporary , in various mediums such as in brass,copper,bronze ,wood ..greet you at the entrance .
The displays are interesting ...
Sneha , the talented artist who is a co- owner of the store has displayed her brilliant paintings too..
Well ! I can say most modestly that I own 7 paintings of hers and a tall wood carving of God Vishnu in a seated posture...I love the stone finish look which Sneha has given to it thus making it look like ...tge old world charm !!
The hanging antique brass diyas in the store have caught my attention and I do plan to buy them .
The statues of Lord Ganesha ,Lord Hanuman and Lord Shiva are crafted in one piece wood by special artisans who hail from across the country offering an insight into the enchanting mythology of our country..the ethic fabric of Indian art is strongly felt whilst one is walking through the gallery .
Each time I visit here I am filled with joy.
Thankyou Sneha for your service at all times .
Your spectacular range of paintings interest me too..!!
